content:
Update, 7:37 p.m. ET: Apple has reported that all service outages are now resolved except for Apple TV.

Apple is currently reporting issues with Apple TV and subscription purchases, with some users also experiencing problems across other services. Here's what we know.

Apple currently lists 8 active issues

Apple's system status page currently shows Apple TV, App Store, Apple Fitness+, Apple Music, Apple Music Subscriptions, Mac App Store, and Subscription Purchase are experiencing outages or other ongoing issues.

According to Apple, most issues began at 4:22 p.m. ET. Apple indicates that the App Store, Apple Music, and Mac App Store are undergoing "routine maintenance and should not impact users," while the Apple TV outage began at 4:43 p.m. ET, with Apple noting the service "may be unavailable due to scheduled maintenance."

During our testing, the Apple TV interface failed to load on iOS, although content still loaded and played normally on other devices.

Top-rated comment from Neil Windard

Apple Fitness stopped my workout halfway through, saying it lost connection with my Apple Watch. I tried several times to reconnect but couldn't find the watch, and even after restarting, it still didn't work, so I gave up.

This outage occurred shortly after various apps — including TestFlight, App Store, and Fitness+ — began displaying internal localization strings in place of normal interface text. It is unclear at this time whether this is related to the other issues Apple is currently facing.

Downdetector reports further confirm Apple TV is impacted, though reports appear to have peaked and are now declining, suggesting the outage may be gradually subsiding.

We will continue to monitor the situation and update this article as more information becomes available or once Apple marks the issues as resolved.

Are you experiencing issues? Let us know in the comments.
